formula: Sales ~ month(Date) + as.numeric(Date - as.Date('2013-01-01')) + Promo + SchoolHoliday + StateHoliday + CompetitionDistance + CompetitionOpenSinceMonth + CompetitionOpenSinceYear + Promo2 + Promo2SinceWeek + Promo2SinceYear + PromoInterval + StoreType + Assortment + (1 | Store) + (0 + as.numeric(Date - as.Date('2013-01-01')) | Store) + (0 + I(as.numeric(Date - as.Date('2013-01-01'))^2) | Store)
notes: RULE GAP: the documented model fits a store x month aggregate, and its time terms are expressions of the datetime column Date, which is ignored since the contract codes no datetime covariate; the random slopes on t and t^2 stay in the formula only. Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.2 and Table 8 (Rossmann: 1.1K stores, 25-31 monthly measures, "Total $ sales (in 100K)", "random terms in t up to a quadratic with no correlations between these terms"); Sigrist 2023 Table 1 and run_experiments.R ((1 |Store) + (0 + t|Store) + (0 + I(t^2)|Store), gpboost with uncorrelated slopes); LMMNN's lme4 baseline (r_scripts/lme4_on_datasets/lme4_rossmann.R) writes (1 + t + I(t^2)|Store), correlated. Preprocessing (rossmann_etl.R in both repositories): daily sales summed per store and month and divided by 1e5, Open, Promo, SchoolHoliday and the StateHoliday dummies summed per month, store data imputed by medians (PromoInterval NA as a level), t = days since 2013-01-01 over its maximum; on this daily table the terms are the same columns per day. BeyondArena keeps open days only and drops Open and Customers; its task has no group_on. DayOfWeek is not a documented term.

formula: log(Income) ~ log(TotalPop) + I(Men/TotalPop) + I(Women/TotalPop) + Hispanic + White + Black + Native + Asian + Pacific + I(VotingAgeCitizen/TotalPop) + Poverty + ChildPoverty + Professional + Service + Office + Construction + Production + Drive + Carpool + Transit + Walk + OtherTransp + WorkAtHome + MeanCommute + I(Employed/TotalPop) + PrivateWork + PublicWork + SelfEmployed + FamilyWork + Unemployment + one county effect per State:County, a Gaussian process with an RBF kernel over the county centroids (lat, long, joined from a county file, not in the table)
notes: RULE GAP: a Gaussian-process spatial random effect has no lme4 form; the county indexes it, so State:County groups (County names repeat across states). Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.3, Table 10 (Income: 71K tracts, 1-2K per location, p = 30, "3K US counties", "Ann. income $ (log)") and Appendix 4 Table 31; r_scripts/ETL/us_income_etl.R and notebooks/spatial/us_income.ipynb (mode spatial, q_spatial = the counties, two spatial variance parameters, no grouped random effect). Preprocessing: joins county centroids by CountyId, divides Men, Women, Employed and VotingAgeCitizen by TotalPop, logs TotalPop, rescales the percentages, keeps counties within latitude 20-50 and longitude -150 to -50, drops rows with any missing value; the network also takes the centroid coordinates as inputs. IncomeErr, IncomePerCap and IncomePerCapErr are dropped by the source.

formula: log(price) ~ year + odometer + manufacturer + condition + fuel + title_status + transmission + drive + size + type + paint_color + random intercept per model + one location effect per lat:long, a Gaussian process with an RBF kernel over the coordinates
notes: RULE GAP: a Gaussian-process spatial random effect has no lme4 form; listings repeat within their coordinates, so lat:long groups beside model. Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.3 and Table 10 (Cars: 97K cars, 12K US locations, categorical model (15K), "Price $ (log)"), notebooks/spatial/cars_spatial_and_categorical.ipynb (mode spatial_and_categoricals: one grouped variance on model_id, two spatial parameters on location_id) and r_scripts/ETL/cars_etl.R: distinct VIN, price 1000-300000, lat 20-50, long -150 to -50, rows without price, year, lat or long dropped, manufacturer cut to the top 10 plus other, NA as a level of every categorical, lat and long rounded to 3 decimals for the location. A further documented GLMM (Sec. 6, lme4_cars_glmm.R: glmer(I(long west of a cut) ~ covariates + price + (1 | model_id), binomial)) takes a recode of long as its response and is not filed. region and state are not documented terms.

formula: y ~ L + K + pop + edu + random intercept per cl + a Gaussian process with an exponential covariance over the region centroids (Long, Lat)
notes: RULE GAP: a Gaussian-process spatial random effect has no lme4 form, and cl has two levels, kept as the documentation fits it random. GPBoost examples/European_GDP_spatial_grouped_data.Rmd at 981e4e4 (Sigrist, GPBoost 1.2.1): 242 NUTS2 regions in 2000 and 2021, y (log) GDP per capita, predictors L, K, pop, edu, Long and Lat the region centroid, group the region id, cl "the cluster the region belongs (there are two clusters)". The linear version: fitGPModel(group_data = data[, c("cl")], gp_coords = data[, c("Long", "Lat")], likelihood = "gaussian", cov_function = "exponential", y = y, X = cbind(1, L, K, pop, edu)); the boosting version uses the same random effects. const is the column of ones, YEAR is not a documented term. The arXiv papers 2004.02653 and 2105.08966 do not use this table.

notes: Pargent et al. 2022 (arXiv 2104.00629) benchmark the encoding of high-cardinality features; their glmm encoder (Sec. 2.7) fits target ~ 1 + (1 | feature) per feature as a target encoder, not a model of the table, so the formula is the reader's. Supplement Table 2: eucalyptus, five classes, high-cardinality levels 12, 14, 16, 27. OpenML 188 (Bulloch 1991, WEKA agridatasets): seedlots (PMCno) of 27 species (Sp) planted at 16 sites (Abbrev) with "mostly three replications of eight trees" in the later trials (Rep), Utility the rating class (none < low < average < good < best, stored unordered). Data Foundry record eucalyptus: "Clustered data per site", tags Non-IID (Grouped). Sites, their replicate blocks and seedlots group; altitude, rainfall, frosts and planting year are site attributes; DBH, Ht, Surv, Vig and the form scores are the measurements Utility rates, ignored as alternate responses, Map_Ref and Latitude site coordinates. Locality (8 regions) is left out.
